fixtures.name: basic-predefined

fixtures.name: compile-error

fixtures.name: asmdef-ref-by-name

fixtures.name: asmdef-ref-by-guid

fixtures.name: asmdef-missing-reference

fixtures.name: asmdef-circular

fixtures.name: asmdef-include-platforms

fixtures.name: asmdef-exclude-platforms

fixtures.name: editor-folder-depth

fixtures.name: plugins-firstpass

fixtures.name: plugins-editor-firstpass
fixtures.description: Editor scripts under Assets/Plugins/Editor compile into Assembly-CSharp-Editor-firstpass, which sees Assembly-CSharp-firstpass and is seen by Assembly-CSharp-Editor; players leave both editor assemblies out.

fixtures.name: standard-assets-firstpass
fixtures.description: Scripts under "Assets/Standard Assets" compile into Assembly-CSharp-firstpass, which Assembly-CSharp references.

fixtures.name: define-constraints-true
fixtures.description: An asmdef whose defineConstraints hold (ENABLE_TELEMETRY from the Standalone scriptingDefineSymbols) is compiled; on Android the constraint fails and it is left out.

fixtures.name: define-constraints-false

fixtures.name: define-constraints-or-not
fixtures.description: defineConstraints ["UNITY_EDITOR || DEVELOPMENT_BUILD", "!DISABLE_DEBUG_TOOLS"]: the assembly exists in the editor and in development players, except where DISABLE_DEBUG_TOOLS is defined (Android).

fixtures.name: version-defines-hit

fixtures.name: version-defines-miss

fixtures.name: version-defines-unity
fixtures.description: versionDefines with resource "Unity" compare against the editor version: 6000.3 (x >= 6000.3) holds only on 6000.3.2f1, [6000.0,6000.1) only on 6000.0.30f1.

fixtures.name: override-references-dll

fixtures.name: override-references-missing

fixtures.name: no-engine-references

fixtures.name: unsafe-allowed

fixtures.name: unsafe-refused

fixtures.name: csc-rsp-define

fixtures.name: csc-rsp-warnaserror

fixtures.name: analyzer-scoped

The unrelated Game.Tools is not analysed (Game.Core itself is not auto-referenced).

fixtures.name: analyzer-global

fixtures.name: api-compat-netfx
fixtures.description: G1. ProjectSettings in the Editor's real shape (wrapped values before the API keys) with Standalone at level 3 (.NET Framework) and editorAssembliesCompatibilityLevel 2, and the System.Memory and System.Buffers NuGet DLLs in Assets/Plugins. Standalone cells compile against unity-4.8-api, where the DLLs' Span<T> and ArrayPool<T> are the only ones; Android keeps the default level 6 (.NET Standard 2.1), which also defines them: CS0433 and CS0121, as in the Editor.

fixtures.name: plugin-native
fixtures.description: G2. An unmanaged x86-64 DLL (no CLI header) under Assets/ThirdParty/Plugins/x86_64 with an ordinary PluginImporter .meta (Editor and Win64 enabled). Unity never passes a native DLL to the compiler: no reference, no CS0009; the script calls it through DllImport.

fixtures.name: precompiled-reference-absent
fixtures.description: G3. An embedded package's Editor-only code-gen asmdef (overrideReferences) lists Unity.IL2CPP.dll, which is in neither the project nor the package, and Vendor.Math.dll, which is. Unity skips a listed name it cannot find without a message and compiles the assembly: ucl reports UCL1004 as info only, references Vendor.Math, and the cell is clean.

fixtures.name: facade-system-runtime
fixtures.description: G4. A package DLL compiled against the System.Runtime contract (Vendor.Contracts) in a project with Standalone at level 3. unity-4.8-api/Facades/System.Runtime.dll forwards its types to mscorlib; under .NET Standard (Android) the NetStandard shims' System.Runtime.dll forwards them to netstandard. No CS0012 in either profile.

fixtures.name: realistic-netfx-nuget
fixtures.description: G1-G4 together, shaped like the maintainer's real project: Standalone level 3, editor level 2, System.Memory, System.Buffers and a System.Runtime-built package DLL in Assets/Plugins, a native x86-64 plugin, and an embedded package whose code-gen asmdef lists a precompiled reference that does not exist. Clean in every cell where the Editor compiles it clean (all Standalone cells, editor and player, development or not).

fixtures.name: test-editmode
fixtures.description: ucl test (phase B): an EditMode suite with pure tests, TestCase and TestCaseSource, a SetUpFixture, cases behind #if UNITY_5_3_OR_NEWER, UNITY_EDITOR and NET_UNITY_4_8, engine-touching tests (needs-unity), [UnityTest], LogAssert, [UnityPlatform] and [RequiresPlayMode] (unity-only), a real failure, ignored, explicit and inconclusive cases, CoreCLR/Mono divergences, a legacy optionalUnityReferences test assembly and a Play Mode assembly. The test framework and com.unity.ext.nunit are embedded stand-ins; nunit.framework.dll is NUnit 3.14.0 from NuGet. 'tests' lists every case ucl test must report, in order, with its category.

fixtures.name: ugui-auto-reference
fixtures.description: Session 3, cause 1. Unity adds UnityEngine.UI (and, in the Editor, UnityEditor.UI) to every asmdef assembly that compiles, except the UI assemblies themselves, the test runners, noEngineReferences assemblies and code-gen assemblies (UnityCsReference AutoReferencedPackageAssemblies). Example.Input lists only "Unity.ugui", a name no asmdef has (as com.unity.inputsystem does), and still sees Selectable, PointerEventData and, in the Editor, UnityEditor.UI.

fixtures.name: editor-builtin-defines
fixtures.description: Session 3, cause 2. The symbols Unity 6 adds that the manual does not list (docs/defines.md, "Built-in symbols", observed in public Unity-generated project files): CSHARP_7_OR_LATER, UNITY_EDITOR_ONLY_COMPILATION, UNITY_INCLUDE_TESTS as a compiler symbol, ENABLE_MONO in every editor cell, and the engine feature and platform sets. A collections-shaped package builds its read-only view differently under ENABLE_UNITY_COLLECTIONS_CHECKS; probe files stop the compile (CS1029) when a rule is broken.

fixtures.name: plugin-same-name
fixtures.description: Session 3, cause 3. Three managed DLLs named System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe.dll: 4.0.4.1 (Auto Reference off) under a package's Runtime/Plugins/CodeAnalysis/, 6.0.0.0 beside a collections package's tests, 6.0.1.0 in an org.nuget package. Unity keeps one precompiled assembly per file name (UnityCsReference PrecompiledAssemblyProvider), the highest assembly version, so every assembly, including Example.Pipeline that lists the name explicitly, gets only the org.nuget copy; UCL1005 (info) names each copy left out. No CS0433 / CS1704.

fixtures.name: package-testables
fixtures.description: Session 3, cause 4. A test assembly (defineConstraints UNITY_INCLUDE_TESTS, or the legacy optionalUnityReferences TestAssemblies) in a package compiles only when the package is embedded in Packages/ or listed in manifest.json "testables" (UnityCsReference CustomScriptAssembly.IsCompatibleWith; manual, "Add tests to your package"): Example.Tools.Tests and Example.Tools.LegacyTests are left out, Example.Lib.Tests (testable) and Example.Local.Tests (embedded) compile. Example.Input.TestFramework, shaped like Unity.InputSystem.TestFramework, is not a test assembly: its UNITY_TESTS_FRAMEWORK comes from its own versionDefines, so it compiles in the Editor; like UnityEngine.TestRunner it stays out of a player unless --include-tests.

fixtures.name: editor-reference-set
fixtures.description: Session 3, cause 5. Editor DLLs Unity passes beyond Managed/UnityEngine/*Module.dll (observed in public Unity-generated project files; UnityCsReference CompilationPipelineCommonHelper): the UnityEngine.dll facade (a vendor DLL built against the single UnityEngine assembly needs it), the active platform's engine module under PlaybackEngines/<support>/Managed (UnityEngine.WebGLModule), in editor cells Managed/UnityEditor.Graphs.dll and every installed platform's PlaybackEngines/<support>/UnityEditor.*.Extensions.dll, and Managed/Unity.CompilationPipeline.Common.dll for Unity.*.CodeGen assemblies.

fixtures.name: analyzer-reach
fixtures.description: Session 3, cause 6 (UnityCsReference RoslynAnalyzers.SetAnalyzers). An analyzer labelled RoslynAnalyzer outside every asmdef folder applies to every assembly, asmdef ones included: here a NuGet-shaped generator under a package's analyzers/dotnet/roslyn4.0/cs/. One under an asmdef folder applies to that assembly and to every assembly that references it directly or through others (Game.UI -> Game.Chat -> Game.Core). The editor's own generators (Tools/BuildPipeline/Unity.SourceGenerators) run on every assembly.

fixtures.name: editor-engine-modules
fixtures.description: Session 4, item 1. A platform's PlaybackEngines/<support>/Managed folder holds its own build of the engine modules, with the same file names as the editor's Managed/UnityEngine/ ones. Editor compiles reference Managed/UnityEngine/ whatever the active platform is, plus only the platform modules the editor folder lacks (UnityEngine.WebGLModule, observed in public Unity-generated project files); player compiles use the platform's copy of each module. The stub WebGL copy of UnityEngine.InputLegacyModule has another version, so referencing both fails with CS1704.

fixtures.name: player-collections-checks
fixtures.description: Session 4, item 2. ucl compiles players against the editor's engine DLLs when the platform folder has no copy of them (PlaybackEngines/<support>/Managed/UnityEngine.CoreModule.dll), and the editor's engine build is made with ENABLE_UNITY_COLLECTIONS_CHECKS: NativeArray<T>.ReadOnly's internal constructor takes the AtomicSafetyHandle (UnityCsReference NativeArray.cs). Such player cells define ENABLE_UNITY_COLLECTIONS_CHECKS too (row E16), so a collections-shaped package binds to the constructor that exists.

fixtures.name: tests-framework-symbol
fixtures.description: Session 4, item 3. Editor compiles define UNITY_TESTS_FRAMEWORK when com.unity.test-framework is installed (here a manifest dependency resolved from the editor, lock source builtin), so a test helper assembly constrained on it (shaped like com.unity.inputsystem's Unity.InputSystem.TestFramework) compiles in the Editor. Players leave test framework assemblies out.
